title: Characterization of the split language
statement: Let $C,c$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{out}$ map pairs of Boolean words to Boolean words, and let $y$ be a Boolean word. There exist words $x,u$ with $y=xu$, $|u|=C(|x|+1)^c$, and $\mathrm{out}(x,u)=[\mathrm{true}]$ if and only if the following holds: if the split solver for $C,c,|y|$ returns no value, the condition is false; if it returns $i$, then $\mathrm{out}(y_{<i},y_{\ge i})=[\mathrm{true}]$, where $y_{<i}$ is the prefix of length $i$ and $y_{\ge i}$ is the remaining suffix.
hypotheses_covered: A function from pairs of Boolean words to Boolean words
